scope: Each coordinate of a q-query circuit’s output amplitude has real and imaginary polynomial representatives of degree at most q (Lemma 4.1).
Distinguishing the two parity classes around any threshold requires N/4 coherent whole-row queries, even when the separation is arbitrarily small.
At arbitrary time t, the evolved endpoint on the selected parity track has Born probability |sin(t/2)|²ᴺ. An estimator accurate to less than half this signal needs at least N/4 row queries.
The endpoint signal before perfect transfer bounds the factorial cutoff using the exponential series and a uniform lower bound on sine.

For coherent access to two incident edge bits per row, any q-query approximation to the evolved endpoint at all scaled times through τ, with absolute probability error ε<1/2, admits a factorial cutoff at most 32q+8.

A single phase oracle encodes the mean of N signs. The parity Fourier coefficient of its evolution can be evaluated exactly, while it vanishes in any compressed circuit amplitude with fewer than N queries.

On these explicitly block-encoded inputs, q controlled phase queries at time budget τ and uniform compressed-amplitude error ε<1 force the least admissible factorial cutoff in Eq. (1) to be at most 8(q+1). The simulator may choose its workspace, input and output frame.
